summary: Conservation is the sole commitment type in Ecuador’s extracted pledges. The first identifies 20% of the territory as protected under different area categories, with the National System of Protected Areas intended to maintain ecosystem coverage and connectivity at terrestrial, marine, and marine-coastal levels. Applied to the reported 256,054 km2 land area, 20% would equal approximately 5.12 million ha, although the commitment is stated as a territorial share. As of December 2022, the SNAP had registered 76 areas totaling 26,208,785.58 ha, a much larger absolute footprint that includes categories extending beyond land. Forest represents 70.3% of Ecuador’s land area, but neither passage specifies how protected areas overlap forests or provides restoration, agricultural, or forest-specific targets.

targets.context: About 5.12 million ha if applied to the reported 256,054 km2 land area; forest covers 70.3% of the country, but no forest-specific allocation is stated.
